clauses.title: Background
clauses.summary: The NDPR is Nigeria's comprehensive data protection regulation issued by NITDA on 25th January 2019. It safeguards critical information infrastructure and protects personal data of Nigerian citizens and residents.
clauses.penalty_info: Non-compliance with NDPR can result in fines up to ₦10M or 2% of annual gross revenue, whichever is greater.

clauses.title: Relationship of the NDPR to the Framework
clauses.summary: The Framework clarifies NDPR provisions. Exceptions include: national security use, criminal/tax investigations, anonymised data processing, and personal/household activities.
clauses.penalty_info: Misapplying exceptions does not shield from enforcement.

clauses.title: Compliance Framework
clauses.summary: Data Controllers must: conduct annual data protection audits, publish privacy policies within 3 months, design data-protection-compliant systems, appoint a DPO if processing 10,000+ data subjects, conduct DPIAs, notify NITDA of breaches within 72 hours, and train staff on data protection.
clauses.penalty_info: Failure to file audit: ₦10,000-₦20,000 filing fees plus potential enforcement action.

clauses.title: Handling Personal Data
clauses.summary: Further processing of personal data beyond the original purpose requires: informing the data subject, obtaining new consent, and ensuring safeguards exist. DPIAs are required for high-impact processing including profiling, automated decision-making, and sensitive data.
clauses.penalty_info: Processing without lawful basis can trigger enforcement proceedings.

clauses.title: Understanding Consent
clauses.summary: Consent must be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous. No implied consent (silence/pre-ticked boxes). Separate consent needed for different data uses. Children under 13 need guardian consent. Cookie consent required. Explicit consent needed for sensitive personal data.
clauses.penalty_info: Processing without valid consent is a direct NDPR violation subject to sanctions.

clauses.title: Data Protection Audit
clauses.summary: Annual data protection audits are mandatory. Organizations processing 2,000+ data subjects must file reports through a DPCO. Filing fees: ₦10,000 (under 2,000 subjects) or ₦20,000 (2,000+). DPCOs must follow strict ethical codes including confidentiality, no conflict of interest, and honesty.
clauses.penalty_info: Filing fees: ₦10,000 for <2,000 data subjects, ₦20,000 for 2,000+. Non-filing triggers enforcement.

clauses.title: Transfer of Personal Data Abroad
clauses.summary: International data transfers require: listing recipient countries, verifying adequate data protection laws, NDPR-compliant privacy policy, encryption details. Transfers to White List countries are permitted. Non-White-List transfers need documented consent per Art. 2.12. Intra-group transfers require BCR or SCC.
clauses.penalty_info: Unauthorized cross-border transfers subject to AGF intervention and enforcement.

clauses.title: Retention of Records
clauses.summary: Data retention periods: 3 years after last active use of digital platform, 6 years after last transaction. Data subjects can request deletion. Data no longer needed must be destroyed per global best practices. Evidence of destruction is a valid defence against breach allegations.
clauses.penalty_info: Improper retention can constitute a breach subject to enforcement.

clauses.title: Data Privacy Breach
clauses.summary: Data breaches must be self-reported to NITDA within 72 hours. Notification must include: breach circumstances, timeline, affected data description, risk assessment, estimated affected individuals, mitigation steps, and contact information. Data subjects must be notified if breach poses high risk.
clauses.penalty_info: Failure to report breaches within 72 hours triggers enforcement and possible prosecution.

clauses.title: Enforcement Framework
clauses.summary: NITDA enforces through: surveillance, complaint filing, investigation, administrative sanctions, and criminal prosecution. Monetary fines based on: nature/gravity of breach, number of affected subjects, damage suffered, unexplored curtailment opportunities, and repeat offence status. Can include service suspension, public warnings, and prosecution referral.
clauses.penalty_info: Fines up to ₦10M or 2% of annual gross revenue. Criminal prosecution possible for national security breaches.

clauses.title: Administrative Redress Panel
clauses.summary: NITDA establishes Administrative Redress Panels (ARP) composed of IT professionals, public administrators, and legal practitioners. ARP decisions are not preconditions for court action. Online dispute resolution is preferred.
clauses.penalty_info: ARP can determine liability of officers.

clauses.title: Third Party Processing
clauses.summary: Data Controllers must publish lists of third parties receiving personal data, including: categories (credit agencies, payment processors), jurisdiction, purpose of disclosure, and data types shared. Third-party processors must comply with NDPR and have written agreements specifying data protection roles.
clauses.penalty_info: Controller liable for third-party processor violations without proper agreements.

clauses.title: Data Protection in MDAs
clauses.summary: All public institutions must comply with the Guidelines for Management of Personal Data by Public Institutions (May 2020). Every PI must publish a privacy policy and designate a DPO responsible for compliance, monitoring, staff training, and NITDA liaison.
clauses.penalty_info: Public institutions subject to same enforcement framework.

clauses.title: Relationship with the Attorney-General
clauses.summary: NITDA coordinates cross-border data transfer decisions with the Attorney-General of the Federation. The AGF may prohibit transfers to countries with inadequate data protection. White List transfers are permitted with NDPR compliance.
clauses.penalty_info: AGF can prohibit transfers and initiate prosecution.

clauses.title: Public Awareness and Capacity Building
clauses.summary: NITDA promotes data protection awareness through seminars, workshops, and conferences in cooperation with industry groups and civil society.
clauses.penalty_info: Lack of staff training can be cited as aggravating factor in enforcement.

clauses.title: Application of International Laws
clauses.summary: Where NDPR does not provide for a principle, the AU Malabo Convention 2014 and EU GDPR and its judicial interpretations have persuasive effect in Nigeria.
clauses.penalty_info: International standards may be applied in enforcement decisions.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Does your app collect personal data (names, emails, phone numbers)?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: Collecting personal data triggers NDPR compliance requirements including privacy policies, consent mechanisms, and data protection audits.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Do you store health, biometric, or other sensitive personal data?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: Sensitive personal data requires explicit consent and heightened security measures under NDPR. Health apps are high-risk.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Do you have a published privacy policy on your app/website?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: A published privacy policy is mandatory within 3 months of business commencement per NDPR Art. 2.5.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Do you transfer user data outside Nigeria (e.g., cloud hosting abroad)?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: Cross-border data transfers require adequacy verification, encryption details, and may need AGF coordination.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Do you have a process to obtain explicit user consent before data collection?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: Valid consent must be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous. Pre-ticked boxes and bundled consent are prohibited.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Does your app target users under 13 years old?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: Processing children's data requires child-friendly privacy notices and guardian consent under NDPR Art. 3.1.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Do you share user data with third-party services (analytics, payment processors)?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: All third-party data recipients must be disclosed, with written agreements specifying data protection obligations.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Do you have a data breach notification process (72-hour reporting to NITDA)?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: NDPR requires self-reporting of data breaches to NITDA within 72 hours with detailed incident information.

questions.text: Did you process the personal data of more than 1,000 Data Subjects in the last 6 months or more than 2,000 in the last 12 months?
Is your top-management aware of the NDPR and the potential implication on your organisation?
Have you implemented any information security standard in your organisation?
Do you have a documented data breach incident management procedure?
Do you collect and process personal information through digital mediums?
Have you organised any NDPR awareness seminar for your members of staff or suppliers?
Have you conducted a detailed audit of your privacy and data protection practices?
Have you set out the management support and direction for data protection compliance?
Do you have a Data Protection compliance and review mechanism?
Have you developed a capacity building plan for compliance with data protection for all members of staff?
Do you know the types of personal data you hold?
Do you know the sources of the personal data you hold?
Who do you share personal data with?
Who is responsible for your compliance with data protection laws and processes?
Have you assessed whether you are a Data Controller or Data Processor?
Have you reviewed your HR policy to ensure personal data of employees are handled in compliance with the NDPR?
Have appropriate technical and organisational measures been implemented to integrate data protection into your processing activities?
Do you have a policy for conducting Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)?
Has a Data Protection Officer been appointed and given responsibility for NDPR compliance?
Have you trained your Data Protection Officer in the last one year?
Is there a clearly available mechanism for data subjects to contact your organisation about personal data issues?
Have you documented your data processing activities?
Have you included an appropriate privacy notice in each data collection process?
Has your organisation recorded legal grounds on which it processes employee data?
Have you identified what personal data is collected and its sources?
Do you have a register of data breaches and security incidents?
Have you carried out a comprehensive review of your processing activities?
Have you reviewed how you seek, record and manage consent?
If your organisation offers services to children, have you communicated privacy information in a clear way a child will understand?
Has your organisation implemented appropriate procedures to detect, report and investigate data breaches?
Have you contracted with any third-party data processors?
Do you transfer personal data to organisations outside Nigeria?
Do you have adequate information systems security (e.g. ISO/IEC 27001)?
